name: Iowa MIS Solo Strings (music-production build)
comment: Recorded by the University of Iowa Electronic Music Studios (Musical Instrument Samples, https://theremin.music.uiowa.edu/MIS.html) in an anechoic chamber, 5 feet from the instrument; the site states that since 1997 the recordings "may be downloaded and used for any projects, without restrictions." Solo violin, viola, cello and double bass, arco and pizzicato, each string recorded chromatically at pp, mf and ff, mono, 16-bit/44.1 kHz. Each note is taken from the string where it is stopped in the lowest position (a semitone over that string's open note up to the next open string; only the lowest open string is used open), or from the nearest string that has it. Violin on program 40, viola 41, cello 42, double bass 43: arco on bank 0 (one preset per recorded dynamic on banks 16-18, legato presets on banks 32-34, each note looped on its steady part), pizzicato on bank 2. Each source file, a chromatic run at one dynamic, is cut into one note per file and every note checked against the run its file is named for (soundbank.py split); then pitch-checked again, intonation offsets within a semitone corrected by fineTune, leading silence trimmed, levels matched per layer with set layer offsets, 16-bit TPDF dither. In build b2 the steady hiss and rumble of every take are reduced by up to 12 dB: a Wiener gain against the noise measured in the quiet frames of each dynamic's takes.
